experiment: Controlled batching vs individual requests, 36 original frozen synthetic cases; unchanged labels/rubric

conditions.isolated: 36 requests/model, one case of state and one identical case question per request
conditions.shared_single: 36 requests/model, identical full 36-case state and one question per request
conditions.batch_forward: 1 request/model, full state and all 36 questions
conditions.batch_repeat: Prescheduled identical repeat, not a retry
conditions.batch_reverse_questions: Reverse question map order only; state bytes unchanged
conditions.batch_reverse_state: Reverse state map order only; forward question order

controls.question_text_and_criteria: Exactly original frozen input.json for all conditions, same explicit partial-list rule
controls.model_routing: Provider-only, fallback disabled; verified response provider/snapshot consistency
controls.schedule: Modes sequential; seeded shuffled mixed-model tasks inside each mode; four client workers. No per-model dedicated throughput test.

limitations: Agent-authored gold labels, no independent human review.
36 correlated simple synthetic cases (12 topics), not long-context real PACBench cases.
Single pass individual conditions; two identical batch passes and one per order perturbation, insufficient to estimate stochastic repeatability or causal order effects.
All 36 cases are unrelated candidate answers. Native PACBench instead often grades multiple claims about one answer; this is a packaging experiment, not a realistic shared-answer workload.
Shared-state comparisons control context; isolated comparison changes context and can change predictions.
Batch questions share state, and outputs need not be statistically independent.
Mixed four-worker scheduling means summed latencies are hypothetical serial service time; window throughput is under mixed contention, not dedicated model throughput.
Modes run in fixed sequence, so cache warming/time effects remain. DS actual cache discounts are recorded, not normalized away.

New DeepSeek comparison is label-only strict-schema with the SAME decision rubric, temperature 0, reasoning off, max_tokens 1024. Earlier exact-flex baseline uses native PACBench prompt, JSON mode, full explanations/recovery/diagnostics and 4096 output cap. Both share model/provider but are different judge protocols.

billing_evidence.interpretation: TypeSafe documents state processed once and additional question tokens charged. Empirical input-token sums confirm savings versus resending full state; no assertion about internal execution independence.
billing_evidence.limits: TypeSafe direct default 64k/request and 32k/question, optional long-context 262k. OpenRouter advertises Jev 262k; not tested at limits. Luna page advertises up to 200 questions. Drex earlier returned 1..16 max. Limits vary by model/route.

validation: All JSON parsed, original case hash unchanged, 304 successful responses, providers verified, credential-pattern check passed
